candidate.answerReason: Equal reading times require Chandra's and Bob's page counts to have ratio 3:2. Chandra therefore reads 3/5 of 760, or 456 pages, agreeing with C.

methods.label: Divide the pages by reading speed
methods.explanation:
Compare how many pages they can read in the same time. In \(90\) seconds, Chandra reads \(90/30=3\) pages and Bob reads \(90/45=2\) pages. Since their rates stay constant, their page counts for any equal reading time must have ratio \(3:2\).

The \(760\) pages must therefore be divided into \(3+2=5\) equal shares. Each share contains
\[
760/5=152\text{ pages}.
\]
Chandra gets three shares, so she reads \(3\cdot152=456\) pages. Bob reads the remaining \(304\) pages. Their reading times agree:
\[
456\cdot30=304\cdot45=13{,}680\text{ seconds}.
\]
Because Chandra begins at page \(1\), reading \(456\) pages means her last page is \(456\). The answer is page \(456\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
